base_case: Over the next 30-60 days the base case is a range-bound-to-choppy consolidation beneath the 6/15 swing high (7,578), with price hovering near the 23.6% fib / valuation-ceiling zone (~7,498-7,544). The mechanical skeleton (50d > 200d, +8.2% over the 200-day) remains intact, but a zero-cushion ERP, Extreme Fear breadth, and wide credit cap upside. Absent breadth/credit confirmation, rallies into the swing-high band are trim opportunities, not chase points.

what_changed_today: CONTINUATION OF SNAP-BACK: close 7,499.36 (~+0.8% from prior ~7,440) extended the recovery, reclaiming the 38.2% fib (7,448), the 50% fib, and now tagging the 23.6% fib (7,498) — price is back within ~1% of the 6/15 swing high (7,578).

MONTE CARLO NEARLY BALANCED: prob_down_first eased to 53.6% (from 65.9% prior) and prob_up_first rose to 46.4% — the down-skew has compressed dramatically, though it still fails all regime thresholds (65/70/75).

ERP EDGED UP TO 0.53%: with forward PE 20.2x against a 10y of 4.42%, the cushion nudged just above the 0.5% ceiling; the 0.5% ERP re-entry floor (7,544) now sits just above spot — price is right at the valuation-confirmed support line.

MFI SURGED INTO OVERBOUGHT: short-timeframe Money Flow Index has driven into the ~85 overbought zone on the bounce, while RSI-14 recovered to the high-50s — a momentum thrust but an MFI trim-zone reading.

BREADTH STILL WEAK BUT LESS EXTREME: McClellan ~899 (still weak/Fear), net new 52-wk highs 1.39% (Fear), safe-haven demand -2.08% and junk spread 1.35% — the 13+ session divergence persists but breadth is no longer at fresh lows.
narrative_summary: A persistent mechanical snap-back has now carried SPX to 7,499, reclaiming the 38.2% and 50% fibs and tagging the 23.6% fib within ~1% of the 6/15 swing high, on a strong top-third close with a benign sub-17 VIX. Yet the rally runs straight into a zero-cushion ERP (0.53%) pinned at the valuation ceiling, an MFI already in the overbought trim zone, and 13+ sessions of Extreme Fear breadth and wide credit that still refuse to confirm the move. The Monte Carlo edge has nearly balanced (53.6% down-first) but fails every regime threshold. In a Late Bull / Topping regime this is a rally into resistance to be trimmed, not chased.
open_questions: Can price clear and hold above the 23.6% fib (7,498) and press the 6/15 swing high (7,578), or does the 89% conditional cascade above 7,578 mark this as the next rejection point?
Will breadth (McClellan ~899) and credit (junk spread 1.35%) finally turn up to confirm the 13+ session price recovery, or does their divergence cap this rally as it has each prior bounce?
With ERP back at exactly the 0.5% ceiling and MFI in the overbought zone, does valuation/momentum exhaustion force another retrace toward the 38.2%/50% fib band?

primary_tension: A persistent mechanical snap-back — reclaimed 38.2%/50% fibs, a tag of the 23.6% fib within ~1% of the 6/15 swing high, a strong top-third close, and a benign sub-17 VIX — is colliding with a zero-cushion ERP (0.53%) pinned at the valuation ceiling, an MFI already in the overbought trim zone, 13+ sessions of Extreme Fear breadth and wide credit that still refuse to confirm, and a Monte Carlo edge that fails every regime threshold — leaving trim bias into strength, not chasing the rally into resistance, as the justified posture.
